## Natural history notes

A small crambid moth characterized by pale yellowish to tan wings marked with darker brown lines and patches, often giving it a delicate, wasp-nest-associated appearance. In Florida, the Wasp Parasitizer Moth occurs around paper wasp colonies in gardens, yards, forest edges, parks, and wooded or semi-open habitats where Polistes and related wasps build exposed paper nests. Adults are nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars develop inside paper wasp nests, feeding on wasp larvae and pupae and spinning silk within the nest cells before pupating.
